title: Pell's Quiet Deal
warm:
Pell's quiet deal meant [player_name] sealed parts of Vivienne's file with Marcus Pell while Crownspire's holding chain preferred silence that still looked like cooperation. Early thirties, she/her, across-the-hall neighbor—she sat in conference hush with Nolan Greer watching from the glass wall like a second verdict while Detective Imani Brooks's homicide interest rose without a body. Four fates open: willing leave, paid vanish, dead, staging. Sealing parts did not force any of them.

"Supervised silence," Pell said, traveling language polished into paperwork. "Not a corpse. Not a confession. Soft alibi stays pliable. Parts of Vivienne's calendar go into a drawer Brooks cannot open without a colder warrant. Soft still means evidence that bends."

Nolan's cufflinks clicked once—the tell that lived when Vivienne's name entered a room—then stilled. Rhea Quinn's slate downstairs still thinned. Unused perfume still breathed from a bath [player_name] should not know. Wind sheer against boardroom glass. Elevator chime late. Soft still meant money's preferred hush.

She catalogued the seal the way Brooks would: NDAs, private-plane language, gaps renamed traveling, neighbor-mistress kept soft enough to wear. Layer 9 made every hush a bargain. Hope and dread shared the hallway. Nolan's eyes found hers through the glass—protective, unfinished, brutal charm scraped honest for a breath.

"Brooks's reckoning spends you into public case with the badge," he said when Pell stepped out. "Pell bargained keeps costly truce and a half-open file. Neither locks Vivienne into one fate. Both spend us into endings that leave four doors open."

Black car at the curb. Wine rings on marble. [player_name] felt the quiet deal fitting her mouth like expensive silk and understood that sealing parts with Pell would change which soft she could still claim—without forcing Vivienne into any single L10 lock.
